recipe: NVFP4 on SM120 with vLLM 0.32.0 and CUDA 12.9: what works with driver 570
note: Fields starting with an underscore are private and removed by check_recipes.py before anything is published.

receipts.value: vLLM 0.32.0 built for CUDA 12.9 runs; vLLM 0.33.0 does not (wheels are built for CUDA 13.0 alone and need torch 2.14)
receipts.caveat: torch 2.14.0+cu130 refused to initialise on driver 570 ("driver too old"). The 0.33.0 release notes state that CUDA 12.9 wheels are dropped. A driver of 580 or newer was not tried.

receipts.value: open kernel module driver 570 reports CUDA 12.8; the CUDA 12.9 wheels run through minor-version compatibility
receipts.caveat: Per the vendor compatibility guide minor-version compatibility stays inside one major CUDA release; the 12.8 system compiler matters (N-05).

receipts.claim: Capability check of NVFP4 linear kernels on the card (compute capability 12.0)
receipts.value: supported: b12x, FlashInfer b12x, FlashInfer CUTLASS, CUTLASS, cuDNN, TensorRT-LLM, Marlin; not supported: CuTe DSL (needs sm_10x)
receipts.caveat: A capability check, no more; not a correctness or speed result.

receipts.claim: Default attention backend on this card and driver
receipts.value: FlashAttention-2 PTX fails ("unsupported toolchain"); Triton attention works; the vision tower also needs the language-model-only flag
receipts.caveat: The serving profile already pins Triton attention.

receipts.claim: Two workarounds for NVFP4 with FlashInfer on the 12.8 system compiler
receipts.value: (a) set the architecture list to 12.0f so FlashInfer uses its ahead-of-time sm120f kernels; (b) turn the FlashInfer autotune warm-up off
receipts.caveat: Without (b) the initial start held 92 GiB for 3.7 minutes and exited with rc=1 after 225 s; with it, start-up took 25 s.

receipts.claim: NVFP4 decode on the card: nvidia/Qwen3-8B-NVFP4, default linear backend
receipts.value: 130.4 / 436.9 / 487.8 tokens/s aggregate at 1 / 4 / 16 streams; start-up 54 s; 5.98 GiB weights
receipts.caveat: Short context (8192), 30% memory fraction, at most 4 sequences in flight, 256 tokens per request, 2 / 8 / 16 requests, one run. The 16-stream figure is therefore queue-limited by the 4-sequence cap.
About +33% at one stream and +26% at 16 against N-06; one run each, so a repeat is needed before calling it settled.

receipts.claim: Five-case answer-format fixture on the NVFP4 8B model
receipts.value: 4 of 5 cases pass; the miss is the same arithmetic case in both backends (reply "1234 + 8765 = 9999", numerically correct but not in the expected format)
receipts.caveat: A smoke test of the stack, not a quality evaluation. No BF16 or FP8 comparison of the same 8B model was run, so no accuracy-loss claim follows.

receipts.claim: Why the 8B model, not the 27B one
receipts.value: the official 27B NVFP4 checkpoint (publisher: Apache-2.0, 21.95 GB) was not downloaded in this run
receipts.caveat: The publisher card claims accuracy within about 1.5 points of BF16 on six tests and says it was tested on a datacentre part, not on this card. None of that is verified here.

receipts.claim: Local NVFP4 quantisation of the 27B with NVIDIA Model Optimizer 0.48.0 (8 calibration samples)
receipts.value: failed 3 times with "Triton Error: device kernel image is invalid" in a PyTorch-native kernel during the calibration forward pass; a fourth attempt failed on a launcher path error
receipts.caveat: Peak card memory 54 GB before the failure; 15 to 23 s each. Cause not isolated (Triton build for this card in the PyTorch 2.13 / CUDA 12.9 stack is the suspect). No NVFP4 27B checkpoint was produced.

receipts.claim: 27B FP8 with MTP-1 in a smoke run on the same stack
receipts.value: 72.2 tokens/s against 43.3 plain on a maximally predictable counting prompt (129 of 129 drafts accepted)
receipts.caveat: An upper bound, not an expected gain; see the Qwen recipe for the real figures.

receipts.value: NVFP4 mixture-of-experts models; NVFP4 KV cache; long context; the 27B model; accuracy against a higher-precision baseline; driver 580 or newer
receipts.caveat: Community reports of broken NVFP4 MoE on this architecture exist; they were not checked here and this recipe says nothing about them.

receipts.value: vLLM 0.32.0+cu129, torch 2.13.0+cu129, transformers 5.19.0, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 (plus cubin and sm120f ahead-of-time cache), b12x 1.5.1, Triton 3.7.1, Python 3.12
